description: HARVALEM WATERFALLS The Harvalem Waterfalls, also known as the Arvalem Waterfalls, is located in the North Goa district of India, near the village of Sanquelim. These picturesque waterfalls are surrounded by lush greenery and make for a scenic spot for visitors. The falls are especially beautiful during the monsoon season when the water flow is at its peak. Surrounded by dense greenery, it offers a tranquil retreat for visitors looking to enjoy nature away from the busier tourist spots. ARVALEM WATERFALLS The Arvalem Waterfalls, also known as Harvalem Waterfalls, are located in the village of Sanquelim in North Goa, approximately 30 km from Panaji. This scenic waterfall is one of the lesser-known yet beautiful natural attractions in Goa. The waterfall is around 50 meters in height and cascades through a lush green landscape, creating a refreshing and peaceful atmosphere, especially during the monsoon season when the water flow is strong. The falls split into two streams, adding to its beauty. At the base, there is a small pond, making it a good spot to relax or enjoy the natural surroundings. HARVALEM WATERFALL GOA The Harvalem Waterfall, also known as the Arvalem Waterfall, is located near the village of Sanquelim in North Goa, around 30 km from Panaji. It is one of Goa’s hidden gems, offering a serene and scenic escape into nature, making it a popular spot for tourists seeking a peaceful experience. HARVALEM WATERFALL INFORMATION Harvalem Waterfall, also known as Arvalem Waterfall, is a serene natural attraction located near Sanquelim in North Goa. Cascading from a height of about 50 meters, the waterfall is most vibrant during the monsoon season, surrounded by lush greenery and offering a tranquil escape for nature lovers. Nearby, visitors can explore the ancient Arvalem Caves, believed to date back to the 6th century, and the Rudreshwar Temple, adding cultural and historical significance to the area. Easily accessible by road, it is an ideal spot for picnics, photography, and a refreshing break from Goa’s beaches.
